pr_semantic_analysis.change_summary: File-drop handling now supports nodes that cannot provide a filesystem Path but can provide an InputStream, including workspace-backed DBNResource files. These nodes are copied into the destination using their display name. Path existence handling also now distinguishes a definitely missing path from one whose existence is indeterminate.

behavior_changes.description: When a dropped node has no Path adapter, the drop operation now attempts to obtain an InputStream and copy its contents into the destination folder under the node's display name; an existing target is replaced.
evidence: The new path-null branch requests an InputStream and delegates to a stream-copy helper.
The helper resolves the display name beneath the destination and uses REPLACE_EXISTING when that target exists.

behavior_changes.description: DBNResource can now adapt an Eclipse IFile resource to an InputStream containing that file's contents. A CoreException while opening the contents is exposed to the caller as a RuntimeException.
evidence: The adapter branch is restricted to InputStream requests for IFile resources.
Successful adaptation returns IFile.getContents(), while failure is wrapped in RuntimeException.

citations.quoted_text: } else if (adapter == InputStream.class && resource instanceof IFile file) {

behavior_changes.description: A dropped Path is now skipped only when it is known not to exist. If the filesystem cannot determine existence, the path can proceed to the later copy or move handling instead of being rejected by this check.
evidence: The new guard uses Files.notExists, which is true only when nonexistence is established.

important_symbols.reason: This is the behavioral integration point that chooses between Path-based copy/move handling and the new InputStream fallback.
It defines destination naming, replacement behavior, and stream-to-filesystem transfer semantics for pathless nodes.
It makes workspace IFile content eligible for the new fallback and defines how content-open failures cross the adapter boundary.

investigation_hints.description: Trace callers of dropNodes and the node types supplied by drag/drop or navigator operations, especially cases where Path adaptation returns null but InputStream adaptation succeeds.
Review the contract for node display names before they are resolved as filesystem paths, including uniqueness, absolute names, separators, and parent-directory segments.
Determine ownership and closure requirements for streams returned by node adapters, and compare exception and cancellation behavior with the existing Path-based transfer path.

local_risks.description: The fallback deliberately replaces an existing destination with the same resolved display name. If display names collide or the destination already contains unrelated content, that content can be overwritten without other conflict handling visible in this path.

If node display names are permitted to be absolute or contain parent-directory components, resolving them directly can select a target outside the intended destination folder; the shown fallback performs no normalization or containment check.

The fallback obtains an InputStream and copies from it without any visible close operation. If adapter callers own these streams, repeated drops or failed copies can retain file or workspace resources.
